wish verb

also I wish, make a wish, if only, three wishes, according to your wishes, wish earnestly

classical

Verg. A. 4.159: optat aprum
Ov. Met. 2.102: sapientius optā
Traupman 408

optō, optāre, optāvī, optātum

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

wish (for); wish someone something

With an object, an infinitive or ut. With a dative, to wish someone something (tibi bona optāvī omnia, Plaut. Rud. 3.2.25), though more often something bad (Lewis & Short). Optā! is “make a wish!”.

Other words

  • utinam — if only …! I wish …

    particle, with the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.1.1; Phaedr. 3.9.7; Traupman 331

    With the present subjunctive for a wish that may come true (utinam veniat!), with the imperfect for one that is not true now (utinam adesset!, I wish he were here).

  • vellem — I wish (that) …, of what is not so

    verb: imperfect subjunctive of volō · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 14.2.4: sed vellem Atticam

    The idiom of Cicero’s letters, with a subjunctive or an accusative.

  • exoptō, exoptāre, exoptāvī, exoptātum — wish greatly; wish someone (a happy birthday)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.118 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 409: Novum Annum laetum tibi exoptō; Traupman 408 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • optātiō, optātiōnis f. — a wish (the act of wishing)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.94: Thēseō cum trēs optātiōnēs Neptūnus dedisset (Lewis & Short); Traupman 408 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • optātum, optātī n. — a wish (the thing wished for)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 408 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • atque utinam continuō ad complexum meae Tulliae, ad ōsculum Atticae possim currere!

    if only I could run straight to a hug from my Tullia and a kiss from Attica!Cic. Att. 12.1.1

  • spūmantemque darī pecora inter inertia vōtīs optat aprum, aut fulvum dēscendere monte leōnem

    and among the tame flocks he wishes a foaming boar might be granted to his prayers, or a tawny lion come down from the mountainVerg. A. 4.158–159

  • sed tū sapientius optā

    but you, wish more wiselyOv. Met. 2.102

  • secundum voluntātem tuam

    according to your wishesTraupman 408

  • Trēs optātiōnēs tibi dō.

    I give you three wishes.Traupman 408

See also happy birthday!, birthday.
